sources.entry: Tiny File Manager - Web based File Manager in PHP, simple, fast and small file manager with a single file. (Demo, Source Code) GPL-3.0 PHP

summary.one_liner: Tiny File Manager is a single-file, web-based PHP file manager for uploading, editing, and organizing files and folders through a browser.
summary.what_it_does: It runs as one PHP file that can be dropped into a web server directory and used to create, delete, modify, view, download, copy, and move files and folders. Uploads are Ajax-based with drag-and-drop, URL imports, and extension filtering. It can create and extract zip and tar archives. Built-in Cloud9 IDE provides a code editor with syntax highlighting, and Google/Microsoft viewers provide previews of PDF, DOC, XLS, and PPT files. Authentication is configured through an $auth_users array, with optional per-user root folders, IP blacklisting/whitelisting, backups, and translations in 35+ languages.
use_cases: browse and edit files on a web server from a browser
upload files to a server with drag-and-drop
manage a lightweight web-hosted file store for a small team
zip or unzip archives on a remote server
edit website code files online with syntax highlighting
preview office documents hosted on a server
how_to_run: Download the ZIP of the latest version from the master branch.
Copy tinyfilemanager.php to your web space.
Open the file in a browser and log in with the default admin/admin@123 or user/12345 credentials.
Before use, set your own username and password in $auth_users (passwords are hashed with password_hash()).
To turn authentication on or off, set $use_auth to true or false.
Optionally place a config.php in the same folder for additional configuration; use the offline branch to avoid CDN resources.
stack: Fileinfo, iconv, zip, tar, mbstring extensions (recommended)
notable: Distributed as a single PHP file with no installation beyond copying it to a directory
Built-in code editor with syntax highlighting for 150+ languages and 35+ themes
Per-user accounts with user-specific root folder mapping
Document preview via Google/Microsoft viewers for files up to 25 MB
Offline branch available for use without CDN resources
caveats: The README cautions against using it as a standard file manager in public spaces and advises removing it from the server after tasks are done.
Default credentials are public and must be changed before use.
Default setup loads front-end libraries from CDNs; an offline branch is needed to avoid that.
